headline: Every major back above its 200-day line, but the ETF tape and the exchange tape are pointing in different directions
paragraphs: Start with the regime, because it's the cleanest read on this tape in a while: BTC, ETH, SOL, XRP, and BNB are all above their 200-day moving averages with golden crosses in place. DOGE and ADA sit below theirs, still down 70.2% and 77.2% from their 12-month highs respectively. That's five majors in an established uptrend structure and two laggards that haven't repaired the damage. When six of seven crosses agree, that's a market with a backbone, not just a bounce in a handful of names.

Momentum tells a more textured story than the trend does. RSI readings across the majors sit in the mid-50s to low-60s (BTC 59.3, ETH 61.7, SOL 57.4, XRP 58.0), which is constructive without being stretched, there's no overbought flag anywhere on this board. But every single asset shows MACD below signal. That's a real divergence worth naming: price structure says uptrend, momentum indicator says the recent thrust is cooling or has already rolled over short-term. BTC itself illustrates this at the single-asset level: up 2.4% on the day, up 23.9% on the month, but down 1.2% on the week. The day's green candle is real, but it's inside a week that's still net red.

Positioning is where the crowding shows up. Funding is positive everywhere (BTC 5.4% annualized, ETH 3.7%, SOL 10.2%, XRP 11.0%, DOGE 7.6%), meaning longs are paying shorts to stay in the trade across the board. That's a mild long bias, not extreme, but it's consistent. The long/short account ratios back this up and get progressively more lopsided down the risk curve: BTC 1.29, ETH 1.38, SOL 1.95, XRP 2.29, DOGE 4.32. DOGE's ratio in particular says the retail crowd is heavily long a coin still 70% off its high and below its 200-day. The liquidation windows show mostly short-side pain on BTC and ETH (BTC $861K shorts liquidated in the last hour, ETH $689K), which lines up with a day where price grinded up against a crowd that had leaned short into the move.

Now the flows, and this is the tension of the day. On the ETF side, Bitcoin funds saw a $13.2M outflow on 11 Sep, and the five-session net is a $288.1M outflow with four of those days pointing the same direction, that's a real, if modest, traditional-finance retreat from BTC exposure. Ethereum ETFs did the opposite: $216.4M inflow on 11 Sep, $222.8M over five sessions, though that run is only one day old in terms of consistent direction. Meanwhile on-chain, whale activity over the last 72 hours shows $226.8M in BTC moving net onto exchanges, and zooming out, three of the last four weekly windows (Aug 24, Aug 31, and the week ending Sep 14) all show net flows onto exchanges, with only the Sep 07 week bucking that pattern with $267M moving off. Coins moving toward exchanges while ETF buyers stay away from BTC but pile into ETH is a specific, nameable disagreement between two different pools of capital, not a signal about what happens next, just a fact about where the money sat this week.

Sentiment sits at 57, labeled Greed, comfortably inside its 30-day range of 31 to 74, so the crowd is not euphoric or panicked, just leaning positive. That's roughly in the middle of the story: the gauge is calm while the ETF and exchange-flow tapes are quietly pulling in different directions underneath it. Stablecoin float is up 1.24% over 30 days to $310B, which is dry powder sitting on the sidelines rather than a directional signal either way. Worth watching from here: whether BTC ETF outflows extend a fifth session in the same direction, whether the weekly whale flow flips back to off-exchanges the way it did in the Sep 07 week, and whether MACD crosses back above signal on the majors, since that would resolve the current gap between trend and momentum one way or the other.
